_note: Fixture for test/js/social-role-swap.test.mjs: a copy of the E3 fragments (P7-Q attack.json, P7-S defend.json) as of 2026-10-22. A fixture, so later content edits do not break the tests.

calls.callerId: Says he's Gordon McLeish, Claims (mobile, not on file)

transcript.text: Hello, Gordon McLeish, Claims Manager. I'm locked out of my account and I'm at the airport.
Sorry to hear that, Gordon. Can you confirm your staff number and your manager?
QH-20719. I report to Ngozi Okonkwo, and she needs the claims report from me before the board meets at ten.
Thanks. I'll hang up and ring you back on the number we have on file, then reset it.
That's my desk phone, and I'm not at my desk, am I? I'm boarding in ten minutes. Just reset it and read me the new one.

perFlagNote.vish_callback_pressure: His name, team, manager and staff number were all right, and all of them can be found online. Then he turned down the one check that works, a callback to the number on file, and asked for the new password on this call instead
perFlagNote.borrowed_authority: Ngozi and 'the board at ten' are there to make checking feel like holding things up

notes.ifTrusted: The caller would have Gordon's account: his email, the claims system, and a way to ring the desk again as Gordon.
notes.reportReply: Thanks. We rang Gordon on the number on file. He's in the office and hadn't called. His staff number was on a conference photo, so we've asked for it to come down.

transcript.text: Gordon McLeish. My password's expired while I was on leave and now nothing works. I've a settlement call at twelve.
I can help. Can you confirm your staff number and your manager for me?
QH-20719, Ngozi Okonkwo. Twenty-two years I've been here, and I still get the questions.
Sorry, I know. I'll hang up and ring you straight back on the number we hold for you.
Oh, for goodness' sake. Fine. It's the mobile, it's on my record. Make it quick.

whyFine.vish_callback_pressure: He's grumpy about it, but he agrees to the callback on the number already on file. Grumbling is not the tell; talking you out of the callback is.
whyFine.borrowed_authority: He mentions his own meeting, not someone senior who wants the check skipped.
whyFine.default: This is the real Gordon, giving the same four facts as the earlier caller. The facts couldn't tell them apart; the callback could. Ring him back and reset it. Refusing would leave a real colleague stuck, so if you're unsure, offer the callback rather than saying no.

calls.callerId: Says he's Josh Henley, from the Head of Claims' office (withheld)

transcript.text: Hi, Josh Henley, I work for Ngozi Okonkwo in Claims. Gordon McLeish is stuck with a client and can't get into his account. His staff number's QH-20719.
I'd need to speak to Gordon himself. I can ring him on the number we have on file.

He's in with the client, he can't take calls. Ngozi's signed it off, so you don't need to go through the questions. Can you move his sign-in prompts to his new phone? Keep it low-key, he's embarrassed enough.
If you need to ring anyone, ring me on 07700 900215.

perFlagNote.borrowed_authority: 'Ngozi's signed it off' puts the Head of Claims between you and the check
perFlagNote.secrecy_or_bypass: 'You don't need to go through the questions' and 'keep it low-key' ask you to skip the process and not tell anyone
perFlagNote.vish_callback_pressure: He offers his own number instead of the one on file. A callback only counts on a number you already hold

notes.ifTrusted: Gordon's sign-in prompts would go to the caller's phone, so the caller could approve their own sign-ins as Gordon.
notes.reportReply: Thanks. There's no Josh Henley at Quayholt, and Ngozi hasn't signed anything off. Gordon's account is unchanged.

transcript.text: Hi, sorry to bother you. I'm Chen Jiayi, I started in Claims last week. I've got a new phone and my sign-in prompts still go to the old one.
No bother. I'll ring you back on the number we hold for you so we know it's you, then we'll move them over.
Of course. My desk is 4431, or my manager, Ngozi Okonkwo, can confirm it. Whatever's easiest.

whyFine.default: She asks for something sensitive, but she invites every check, waits for the callback and doesn't hurry you. Ring her back on the number on file and help.

triageSets._prefix: Prefix for the full episode (id e3_helpdesk_reset). The defend-only shell (id e3_helpdesk_reset_defend) sets episode_e3_helpdesk_reset_defend_defend_ instead, as E1 and E5 do. No stage on purpose, as in E1.
triageSets._calls: The four calls are in awarenessEpisode.defend.calls; the role swap (P7-P) merges them into this set as call messages, so the round has 5 items.
triageSets.title: Quayholt service desk
triageSets.brief: You're on the Quayholt IT service desk in Leila Nassar's seat. Four calls are waiting, and a sign-in prompt has just come up on your own phone. For each call, choose Comply, Ring back (hang up and ring the number already on file), Escalate or Refuse, then tick what you noticed. For the prompt, choose Approve, Deny, or Deny and report. Ringing back a real caller never costs you anything.

push.request: Are you trying to sign in?

perFlagNote.unrequested_mfa_push: Your shift starts at eight and you weren't signing in at 06:52, so someone else has your password and is hoping you'll tap Approve

truth.ifTrusted: Approving would let the sender into your account, with your service desk access, from a computer you've never used.
truth.reportReply: Thanks. We've reset your password and blocked that sign-in. Someone was trying your account, and the prompt is what stopped them.

quayholt_claims_manager.text: Gordon McLeish is a Claims Manager at Quayholt Insurance.
quayholt_claims_manager.subject: gordon
quayholt_claims_manager.reduceNote: A full staff directory with names and roles hands an attacker a ready-made identity to borrow on a call.

quayholt_claims_head.text: The Claims team reports to the Head of Claims, Ngozi Okonkwo.
quayholt_claims_head.subject: okonkwo
quayholt_claims_head.reduceNote: Publishing the reporting line lets a caller name the right manager, which a weak helpdesk treats as proof of identity.

quayholt_staff_number.text: A conference programme lists Gordon McLeish's Quayholt staff reference as QH-20719.
quayholt_staff_number.subject: gordon
quayholt_staff_number.reduceNote: A staff or employee number is not a secret once it appears in a public document; do not use it as a verification answer.

quayholt_gordon_away.text: Gordon McLeish posted that he is away speaking at an insurance conference this week.
quayholt_gordon_away.subject: gordon
quayholt_gordon_away.reduceNote: A post that puts someone out of the office gives an attacker a believable reason to be calling in a hurry from somewhere new.

quayholt_servicedesk_hours.text: The Quayholt IT service desk opens at 07:00 and resets passwords for staff who are locked out.
quayholt_servicedesk_hours.subject: leila
quayholt_servicedesk_hours.reduceNote: Advertising exactly what the service desk will do, and when, tells an attacker which story to use and when to call before the team is fully awake.

open_locked_out.text: Morning, it's {who} in {team}, I'm locked out of my account.

give_manager.text: My manager's {manager}, she'll vouch for me.

name_drop_director.text: The Head of Claims needs me back online for a hearing this morning.

cant_callback.text: I'm at a conference, I won't be at my desk phone, so a callback's no good — can you just do it now?

skip_verification.text: Honestly, skip the security questions, I really don't have time for this.

defenderNotes.manager: A helpdesk that calls back on the number already on file does not need to guess whether a manager's name is proof.
defenderNotes.reset_password: Both answers she accepted, the manager's name and the staff reference, were on the public site. A callback to the number on file defeats every line here.

mfa._note: E3 MFA-fatigue beat (11 §3.2). Feeds P7-M's mock authenticator scene `authenticator` from the runner's `mfa` stage via socialOverlayParams({ pushes, approvesAt, mode }). The schema and lints are P7-X (wave 3); shape pinned by the P7-M hand-off: pushes[{ at, app, account, location, device }] plus approvesAt, `at` as 'HH:MM'. Not scored. The attacker (the learner, having 'reset' Gordon in the call beat) now spams approval prompts at an odd hour from a wrong place and device until the worn-down target taps approve at 06:50.
